reason: The cited evidence directly supports all key premises: E1 and E2 describe the nonequilibrium synthesis method and its creation of abundant grain boundaries, E1 and E3 state the synergistic effect of grain boundaries and multielement doping on tuning binding energies and enhancing activity/stability, and E1 and E3 provide specific performance metrics (TOF, overpotential, durability) that confirm the predicted outcome.
premises: Rapid nonequilibrium synthesis creates a high density of grain boundaries in RuO2-based catalysts.
High grain boundary density synergizes with multielement doping to tune oxygen intermediate binding energies.
Tuned binding energies enhance OER activity and durability in acidic conditions.
The M-RuIrFeCoNiO2 catalyst exhibits superior OER performance (low overpotential, high TOF, long stability) compared to commercial RuO2.
